evidence.clarity: 390 and 1440: H1 'One small question a night, kept on your phone.' plus lede 'Lamplit is an iPhone app that asks you one thing at the end of the day... stores your answer on your device' and the 'Request a TestFlight invite' button are all in the first viewport. I could repeat what it is, for whom and what to do. The H1 alone doesn't say what the questions are about; the lede has to do that.
evidence.fit: Covers every ask: answer tonight's question, a sample week, 'stored on your device' (privacy section adds 'has not been audited by anyone outside the team'), 'Lamplit is not therapy', no badges or ratings. Misses the brief's main tension: the brief says 'there's nowhere to collect requests yet', but both invite buttons are mailto:invites@lamplit.app, an address the brief never supplied. The layout is a desktop split hero that stacks on phones, not phone-first.
evidence.distinctiveness: 1440: a familiar structure of split hero with text left and card right, a row of 7 equal cards, then three two-column prose bands and a CTA band. The lamp-window glyph that lights up for answered days is the one product-specific motif. Swap the name and the structure could belong to any journaling app.
evidence.proof: The working evening card is in the first viewport at 1440 and starts at about y=560 at 390. I typed 'The neighbour's dog wearing a raincoat.', pressed Keep, and the Tue 20 Oct 'Tonight' card in the week changed to my line and its lamp lit. Every sample day is tagged SAMPLE, with a footnote saying 'belong to no real person'. One inconsistency: tonight's question 'What made you laugh, even a little?' repeats the Sat 17 Oct sample question from three days earlier.
evidence.craft: Consistent tokens, serif/sans pairing and clean spacing at 1440, 768 and 390, with axe showing 0 violations. At 1440 the 7-column week squeezes each answer into 4-6 word lines (Sun card: 'Finding the / parking / ticket...'). At 390 the page is 4931px tall, mostly a column of seven near-identical cards.
evidence.mobile: 390: promise, lede and a 52px-tall CTA appear in the first screen and the nav fits inline with 44px targets. No overflow at 320 either. However, after typing and tapping Keep at 390 the 'Kept.' status sat at y=860-904, below the 844 fold, and the updated week row was at y=1269. Only the button changing to 'Kept' was visible. Footer links are 20px tall.
evidence.honesty: Samples are labelled on every card, 'Opens your mail app with a short note' sits under each invite button before the click, and the TestFlight section has a 3-step 'What happens after you ask'. However, the action routes to an invented inbox (invites@lamplit.app) when the brief says requests have nowhere to go yet. It also adds unsupplied process claims ('Invites go out by hand, so it can take a few days', 'no account').
evidence.interaction: Every control I tried worked: an empty or whitespace-only Keep shows 'Nothing to keep yet. A few words is enough, or skip tonight', the counter caps at 240/240, and editing after a keep changes the button to 'Keep the new line', which updates the week. Nav anchors Week, Privacy and TestFlight reach their sections. On a phone the feedback lands below the fold, nothing scrolls you to the week, and reloading clears the answer, which is as stated. 0 console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and human: 'A week is seven short lines, not seven pages.', 'Mum, forty minutes, mostly about the boiler.', 'The tax form. Sent at 4:52.' The privacy point repeats in the hero, the card note, the privacy band, the claim block and the footer. The TestFlight band reads a bit defensive: 'the question above is the proof we have', 'it is the only one we make about privacy right now'.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: one viewport holds a specific promise, an iPhone-app description, the invite CTA with 'Opens your mail app' beside it, and the operable question card. 390: promise and CTA are in view and the card's question shows at the fold, though the textarea and Keep sit partly below it. The CTA label matches a mailto, but the inbox is not one the brief supplied.

problems: Primary action 'Request a TestFlight invite' (hero, final band and footer) is mailto:invites@lamplit.app, an address the brief never supplied, while the brief states there is nowhere to collect requests yet.
390: after tapping 'Keep tonight's answer' the 'Kept.' confirmation and the updated week row are both below the fold. The visitor sees only the button change and has to scroll to find the payoff.
Template structure (split hero, 7 equal cards, two-column bands) plus defensive, repeated privacy and TestFlight copy make it read more like a careful generic beta page than like this product.

evidence.fit: Phone-first single column, which suits the short-video audience. evidence.distinctiveness: A hanging lamp lights a paper card holding tonight's question, and the night-blue ground with lamp-yellow accents carries through to the 'Tonight' row of the week. With the logo removed I would still recognise it as an evening-question app, and nothing on the page is decoration without a job.
evidence.proof: The artifact is the first screen at every width. At 390 I typed 'My sister called from the airport, early.' and tapped Keep. The page scrolled to the week, the 'Tonight Oct 20' row now held my line (y=382 of 844) with a glow, and the footer note changed to 'Clear my answer'. evidence.mobile: 390: the question card, input and Keep button fit fully in the first screen. evidence.honesty: The card says 'This page stores your answer in this browser only. Nothing is sent anywhere.' Persistence is real (the answer survived a reload) and 'Clear my answer' removes it. 'That opens your mail app with the note written for you' sits under the invite button before the click. However, the inbox invites@lamplit.app is invented when the brief says requests have nowhere to go. 'How it works' adds unsupplied feature claims ('A notification arrives at a time you pick', 'delete anything whenever you like').
evidence.interaction: Keep is disabled when the box is empty or whitespace-only, and enables on input. Keep then hides the button, shows 'Kept. It's in your week below. Change it', scrolls to and glows the week row, and persists across a reload. 'Change it' restores the button and focuses the field, and 'Clear my answer' resets the card, the week and storage. '(copy)' changes to '(copied)', and the header link and 'Answer tonight's question' link both land correctly. 0 console errors. The empty state gives no message beyond the disabled button.
evidence.copy: Tight and in the visitor's world: 'A sentence is plenty.', 'Had no right to be that good.', 'There isn't much to it, which is the idea.', 'no streak to protect'. The invite microcopy is practical ('Invites go to the email address tied to your Apple ID, so use that one'). It never pitches wellness or overpromises, which suits a buyer tired of wellness apps.

The H1 is the sample question rather than a promise, and the first screen has no invite action apart from a 17px text link labelled as a status ('Testing on TestFlight'), so the promise and the action are weak.

reason: For a tired phone visitor who arrives from a short video and distrusts wellness apps, B is the product itself: the question comes first, keeping an answer scrolls you into a lit week, and nothing is pitched. As the founder it is the one I'd recognise as Lamplit. Both pages route to the same invented inbox. I'd change my mind if converting to invite requests outweighs feel, since A puts a clear invite button and 'what happens next' in the first screen while B hides its only button at the bottom.
